sections.title: Identifiability
sections.text:
5 observation(s) of 3 parameter(s): rank 1, so 1 independent combination(s) of the parameters are determined and 2 are not. Not one parameter is separately identifiable: every one of them can be traded against another without moving any observation. What the observations cannot separate:   - no observation here responds to reaction_Ki on its own -- its column of the matrix cannot be told from zero at this run's threshold -- so it cannot be recovered from these observations at any precision, however good the data are   - only the ratio reaction_kcat/reaction_Km is determined; reaction_kcat and reaction_Km are not separately identifiable from these observations Those 2 directions are one orthonormal basis of the unrecoverable subspace and not the only one; any rotation of them describes the same set. The per-parameter verdict above does not depend on the choice, so read that as the finding and these as an illustration of it. 4 observation(s) respond to nothing at all above their own noise floor: steady state of reaction_S, steady state of reaction_P, steady state of reaction_E, steady state of reaction_I. They contribute no rank, so removing them from the experiment would cost nothing. Singular values [1.41, 0, 0] against a threshold of 8e-05, which is the radius of the error ball the rows' own declared accuracies put around this matrix -- below it a singular value cannot be told from zero. Evaluated at reaction_kcat=100, reaction_Km=0.03, reaction_Ki=0.0014. Local and practical, not structural: this is the rank of one finite-difference matrix at one point, for these observations. A rank deficiency found here is real evidence that these observations do not separate the parameters it names. Full rank is not proof of identifiability -- it rules out neither a deficiency elsewhere in parameter space, nor a global ambiguity no local method can see, nor a direction that real measurement error would swallow.

Asked about the 3 constant(s) the literature could supply, not about the starting amounts. A concentration is a choice rather than something a measurement recovers, and including one would invent a degeneracy nobody is trying to break.

sections.title: Robustness to the placeholders
sections.text:
'exactly one stable state' held in every one of the 5 sample(s) evaluated, with 1 parameter(s) varied log-uniformly over +/-1 decade(s) around the model's current values (seed 0). Every draw was judged by a steady-state search from 8 starting point(s) per species. A conclusion about how many stable states exist is an answer from a search, and a shallower one finds fewer -- so a fraction produced at one depth cannot be compared against a headline produced at another. This is a count over a stated box, not a probability. The box is a range chosen for want of a measured one, so surviving it is evidence about the mechanism and failing it is evidence about how much the answer rests on numbers nobody has measured -- neither is a proof, and a conclusion that survives every sample here may still fail just outside.

The conclusion resampled -- 'exactly one stable state' -- is the one this model's own steady-state search produced, not a fixed question asked of every model. Asking a monostable model whether it stays bistable returns a true 0% about something nobody claimed.

sections.title: Cross-checks
sections.text:
Cross-checked michaelis_menten_with_a_competitive_inhibitor: 5 agreement(s), 0 contradiction(s), 1 divergence(s), 1 check(s) that did not run. DIVERGENCES -- differences with a reading that is not a bug, reported because the reading is itself information:   - [divergence] settling time / reaction_E=0.001, reaction_I=9.861e-32, reaction_P=1, reaction_S=-2.924e-16: the trajectory is still 0.768 of its initial deviation away after t=2.4, which is 8 times the predicted settling time of 0.3, so no settling time could be measured. It is approaching, and more slowly than the linearisation says. DOUBT: the linearisation as a description of THIS approach, not the eigenvalue arithmetic. An eigenvalue is a statement about the neighbourhood of the fixed point, and a trajectory that spends its time far away is not governed by it. The consequence worth acting on is in `simulate.choose_window`, which multiplies this same settling time by SETTLING_MULTIPLES to pick a plot window: on this model that window cuts the approach off, and the curve will look as though it had finished. 1 check(s) did not run, which is not the same as passing: sensitivity (no quantity was named. A sensitivity cross-check needs a scalar to differentiate, and choosing one here would choose which of this model's conclusions gets checked without saying so. Pass `species=`). 4 of 5 checks produced a result (dimensions, conservation, fixed point, settling time). Every one of them compares Caterva against Caterva. Agreement means the package is self-consistent here, not that the model is right: the routes share the rate laws, the stoichiometry and the parameter values, so a mechanism written down wrongly is reproduced faithfully by all of them.

No species was named, so the sensitivity cross-check did not run. Pass --rank-against SPECIES to choose the quantity it differentiates -- choosing one here would pick which of this model's conclusions gets checked without saying which.
